subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity SKU allocation, throughput targets & rollout roadmap
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlas-systems.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlas-systems.com, infra@atlas-systems.com
Date: 2028-06-13T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Atlas RFP - dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire (clarifications)

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the initial RFP materials — we reviewed the questionnaire and have a few clarifying items before our procurement committee finalizes the ask. Attached is Atlas_RFP_Dedicated_Capacity.xlsx with our expected workload shapes. Key clarifications we need from Redwood: 

1) SKU mapping: can you confirm equivalent SKU names for H100 vs A100 variants and recommended NVLink / multi-GPU packing guidance?
2) Throughput targets: we provided top-line concurrent users and mixed workload tps in the spreadsheet — we'd like a recommended committed GPU mix that meets 99th percentile tail latency <= 500ms for interactive chat use cases and throughput headroom for batch generation.
3) Reservation model: explain how burst lanes or overage works when committed capacity is saturated — is preemption used, and do we get predictable fallback to cheaper model variants?
4) Compliance / evidence: where in the runbook can we find audit log retention and encryption sections for private deployments (we're evaluating Private VPC option).

Can we get answers inline in the spreadsheet, plus a short 30–45 minute technical workshop next week to walk the sizing?

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering
Atlas Systems

Attachments: Atlas_RFP_Dedicated_Capacity.xlsx
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlas-systems.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas RFP - dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire (clarifications)

Hi Liam — thanks for the workbook and the clear asks. I validated the workload shapes with our serving team and filled the workbook with line-by-line notes; attaching the updated workbook and our capacity runbook excerpt. Summary answers inline below and a short sketch of a recommended initial commitment.

Quick answers (tl;dr):
- SKU mapping and packing: H100 (H100-SXM) recommended for latency-critical chat when you need single-GPU low-latency and very large context (>=64k). A100-80GB (A100-SXM-80) is our go-to for steady high-throughput generation and heavy KV cache workloads. L4-class (L4/RTX equivalent) is cost-efficient for embeddings and low-compute inference. For NVLink: prefer 2x NVLink pairs per multi-GPU Pod for models that can span GPUs; otherwise single-GPU instances maximize scheduling density.

- Baseline committed mix (recommended starting point):
  * Latency-critical chat: 8 x H100 GPUs (reserved) — target concurrency: 600 active chat sessions, expected 95th token latency sub-200ms for 4k contexts; p99 under loaded test ~420–500ms depending on prompt size.
  * High-throughput generation / batch: 16 x A100-80GB GPUs (reserved) — designed to sustain large-batch token throughput for offline job queues and long-running generations.
  * Embeddings & reranking: 24 x L4-class GPUs (reserved) — optimized for high-QPS embedding workloads at low cost.

- Headroom & burst: we recommend a burst lane of up to 40% additional capacity (on-demand allocation) for seasonal spikes. When committed pool is saturated, requests are routed per your policy: (1) to burst (if available), (2) to a compatible quantized model variant, or (3) queued with best-effort latency. No preemption of your committed jobs unless you opt into a shared-fallback plan; by default committed reservations are isolated.

- Fallback model variants: we can route to an INT8-quantized variant of your primary model family or to a smaller family with matched prompt templates. We include automated quality-weighted rollout checks so you can limit fallback only to non-critical routes.

- Compliance/runbook pointers: the attached redwood_capacity_runbook_v1.pdf includes sections 3.2 (audit log retention — default 365d, configurable), 4.1 (KMS integrations and HSM support), and 5.3 (Private VPC operational checklist). If you need an SOC 2 package and evidence bundle, we can provide our full compliance repo under an NDA.

Workshop: we have availability on Tue/Wed next week. Propose Wed 2028-06-21 10:00am PT — I'll invite the engineering owners from our sizing team.

I've also included a conservative cost note for the baseline mix in the workbook and a suggested A/B canary plan for the first 6-week deployment. Let us know if you want us to prepare a side-by-side runbook of quantization tradeoffs (INT8 vs FP16) for each critical route.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Atlas RFP - dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire (commercial + SLA notes)

Looping in a commercial note and next steps on contracting. Vanessa — excellent technical answers. A couple of commercial carve-outs to flag for the procurement team: 

- Pricing construct: committed monthly GPU-hours + an on-demand burst rate. We'll include a blended effective rate for the initial 12-month term with step-downs at 6/12 months based on utilization thresholds.
- SLA and credits: standard Dedicated SLA targets will be 99.95% availability for reserved pools. Tail-latency objectives are treated as performance targets (operational SLO) and will be documented in the acceptance test plan; credits are available only for availability SLA misses, not performance.
- Contracting items: procurement should expect a 6-week onboarding window to stand up private control plane + network peering, and a standard security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence pack will be attached to the contract.

I've created the initial commercial summary and uploaded the draft SLA_T&Cs_v2.docx to the drive link below — please review and we'll prepare the DocuSign in parallel.

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-Atlas-RFP

Vanessa / Ben — thanks for the thorough answers and the workbook updates. A few follow-ups before the workshop: 

- Can you add an alternative reduced-cost configuration that assumes more aggressive quantization (INT8) and a fallback policy that prioritizes only non-interactive routes? We'd like to compare total cost of ownership at 75% committed utilization vs 95% committed utilization.
- Please include an estimated onboarding timeline that breaks down tasks (network peering, KMS key exchange, acceptance testing, model onboarding). We need that for our procurement gating.

Wed 2028-06-21 10:00am PT works for us — please send a calendar invite with dial-in and workshop agenda. We'll have the infra engineering lead (infra@atlas-systems.com) join.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Regards,
Liam
